tagline: Elephant country, Khmer temples, and the handwoven silk of southern Isan
introHtml: Surin is a southern Isan province where most people think of elephants first. It's home to elephant villages where families have raised elephants for generations, and to a big annual elephant show that's known across the country. Beyond elephants there are Khmer temples scattered along the border, hand-loomed silk in old patterns woven by whole villages, and garlic and jasmine rice that the province is famous for. If you like travel where you actually see how local people live, Surin is a place to take slow and just soak in the atmosphere.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable, which lines up with the elephant show in mid-November

highlights.name: Ban Ta Klang Elephant Village
highlights.blurb: One of Thailand's largest elephant-keeping villages. The Kuy people here have been bonded with elephants for ages — come watch the mahouts' way of life and feed the elephants up close.

highlights.name: Surin Elephant Round-Up
highlights.blurb: The annual show in mid-November that brings hundreds of elephants together to perform. It's the event the town is known for, and people from all over the country plan trips around it.

highlights.name: Prasat Sikhoraphum
highlights.blurb: Surin's most beautiful Khmer temple — five brick prangs, famous for the finely carved apsara lintel.

highlights.name: Ban Tha Sawang Silk
highlights.blurb: A village that weaves gold-brocade silk in old patterns, and has woven cloth for important national occasions. The fabric is dense and the patterns are intricate.

highlights.name: Chong Chom Border Crossing
highlights.blurb: The Thailand–Cambodia crossing in Kap Choeng district, with a border market where you can shop around and get a feel for both sides.

highlights.name: Surin Garlic and Jasmine Rice
highlights.blurb: The province's signature products — small, strong-smelling garlic cloves, and Thung Kula jasmine rice that people take home as a gift.

foodScene.name: Southern Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken — bold Isan flavors you can find all over town. Some places near the border carry a faint Khmer touch.

foodScene.name: Surin jasmine rice
foodScene.note: Jasmine rice grown in the Thung Kula Ronghai plains in the province. It cooks up fragrant and soft, and people buy it home by the sack.

foodScene.name: Pickled garlic
foodScene.note: Surin's small, strong garlic cloves, pickled or made into a take-home treat. It pairs well alongside Isan food.

foodScene.name: Local pla som and naem
foodScene.note: Local fermented fish and pork with a mellow sourness. Fry it up with hot steamed rice, or buy it as a gift to take home.

foodScene.name: Khanom jeen nam ya pa
foodScene.note: A local favorite — a rich curry-paste sauce over rice noodles, eaten with a big pile of fresh vegetables.

foodScene.name: Kuay jab yuan
foodScene.note: A Vietnamese-influenced dish you can find in town — soft wide noodles in a clear broth, topped with pork and fried garlic.

foodScene.name: Cafes and evening markets in town
foodScene.note: The town center has little cafes and an evening market by the railway, with street food and snacks to graze on after dark.

attractions.name: Ban Ta Klang Elephant Study Center
attractions.blurb: The Kuy people's elephant village, with an elephant museum and activities to learn the long-standing way of life of the mahouts.

attractions.name: Prasat Sikhoraphum
attractions.blurb: A well-preserved Khmer temple of five brick prangs, with a finely carved apsara lintel as the highlight.

attractions.name: Prasat Ta Muen Thom
attractions.blurb: A group of sandstone Khmer temples right on the border in Phanom Dong Rak district, set on the ancient route into Cambodia.

attractions.name: Ban Tha Sawang Silk Weaving Village
attractions.blurb: A community that weaves gold-brocade silk in old patterns. Watch the weaving on hand looms and pick up quality silk.

attractions.name: Phanom Sawai Forest Park
attractions.blurb: A low hill near town with a large Buddha image and viewpoints — a spot where Surin locals come to relax.

attractions.name: Huay Saneng Reservoir
attractions.blurb: A wide reservoir near town with a road along the dam crest for cycling and catching the cool evening breeze.

attractions.name: Chong Chom Border Market
attractions.blurb: The Thailand–Cambodia border market in Kap Choeng district, where you can browse for unusual finds and cheap goods from both sides.

attractions.name: Phraya Surin Phakdi Monument
attractions.blurb: The monument to the town's first governor in the center of Surin, with an accompanying elephant figure — a city landmark.
